comment: Keyring authority rotation. Each case starts from an approved source whose authority came from an initial keyring (initialTrusted/initialRevoked, signed by the reviewed pin), optionally applies an accepted intermediate keyring (via: version, trusted, revoked, signedBy), then republishes the keyring. PIN, ROT and OLD stand for the fingerprints below; ARCH stands for an unrelated global signing key (an Arch/CachyOS or administrator key). pacman-key --populate applies the revoked list to the shared keyring, so a revocation may name only a key this source has actually used: the pin, an earlier revocation, or an observed signer (a primary whose VALIDSIG verified this source's database or keyring archive). A fingerprint merely listed in a trusted list, now or in an earlier archive, is never revocable. signedBy: pinned (PIN), rotated (ROT), old (OLD).
